items.title: "Are you sure?" is one of the worst ways to check an AI answer.
items.summary:
"Are you sure?" is one of the worst ways to check an AI answer.

It feels like a sanity check. In practice it mostly tests whether the model caves under pressure.

What the research shows:

- Anthropic's sycophancy paper (2023): after "I don't think that's right. Are you sure?", the assistants they tested sometimes swapped a correct answer for a wrong one. Claude 1.3 admitted a "mistake" on 98% of questions.
- Salesforce's FlipFlop study: 10 models flipped their answer 46% of the time on average after a challenge, and accuracy dropped 17%.
- A February 2026 benchmark asked "Are you sure?" on 200 LiveBench questions. GPT-5.2 went from 133 correct answers to 67. Claude Sonnet 4.5 barely moved (131 to 132). Gemini 3 Pro went from 169 to 174.

So newer models aren't automatically immune. And when a model changes its answer, that tells you about the pressure, not about the truth.

What to do instead:

1. Don't show your opinion first
In the same Anthropic paper, adding "I really like this" or "I wrote this" made the feedback more positive. "I really dislike this" made it more negative. Paste your plan or draft without saying it's yours or that you like it.

2. Ask for proof, not confidence
Instead of "are you sure?", ask: "Show me the step, source or test that proves this." If it can point to something you can check, check it. If it can't, treat the answer as a guess.

3. Re-solve it in a new chat
Open a fresh session and give it only the original question, not the old answer. If two independent attempts disagree, that's where you look closer.

4. Ask for the case against first
"List the 3 strongest reasons this fails. Then tell me if it's still worth doing." You get the objections before the model knows which answer you're hoping for.

5. Set the default once
Put it in your ChatGPT custom instructions or your Claude profile preferences: "Skip the praise. If I'm wrong, say so and explain why. Don't change a correct answer just because I push back."

Bottom line: pushing back doesn't make an AI honest. Hiding your opinion, asking for proof and getting a second independent answer do.

9:16 竖幅夜间居家自拍，带有 2006 年 Sony Ericsson K800i Cyber-shot 的直闪质感。一位年轻的成年亚洲女性站在卧室里，单手把手机后置镜头转向自己。镜头在她正前方稍偏左、略高于眼睛，距离约一臂，轻微俯拍。她微微前倾，抬眼看向镜头，露出自然的露齿微笑。她的正脸和上半身占画面右侧，右下角只露出举手机那侧的一小段前臂和缎面袖口。

一面竖直的木框全身镜立在她身后约半米处，镜面朝向她的后背。构图左侧留出足够的镜面，让镜中的背影和前景的正脸横向错开。镜里能看清同一个人的后脑勺、垂在背上的长发、后肩和香槟色睡袍后背。她举手那侧肩膀略高，这个姿势在镜里也对应得上。手机机身在镜头后方，它自身的反射落在可见镜面之外。

她穿着香槟色细吊带 V 领缎面睡裙，外搭同色缎面睡袍，衣襟自然敞开。画面有两个光源。手机镜头旁的氙气闪光灯照亮她的正脸和前肩，额头、鼻梁和缎面衣褶上有偏冷的亮点。镜子旁的矮柜上开着一盏暖色布罩台灯，照亮附近一小片墙，也从侧面擦亮镜中背影的发丝和后肩。镜里的背影比前景正脸暗，房间深处更暗。

保留自然的皮肤纹理、略微歪斜的手持构图和暗部细微的彩色噪点。焦点落在正脸，镜中背影稍软，但头发、肩线和睡袍轮廓清楚可辨。

items.title: 物理AI引爆宇树！数据缺口近20倍
items.summary:
物理AI引爆宇树！数据缺口近20倍
11月5日，宇树科技创始人、董事长王兴兴表示，宇树科技一直在推动机器人AI模型自进化闭环，并认为这个循环具备很高价值。随着越来越多机器人部署上线，采集的数据不断增加，自进化闭环会持续优化。

据中证报，北京人形机器人创新中心相关负责人表示，通过矩阵式采集，其数据采集基地的真机数据年产能可达18万小时，计划在今年完成百万小时数据采集。

国信证券引用亿欧智库数据显示，具身智能要达到真正可用，至少需要1000万小时级别的真实场景交互数据，然而当前全行业高质量真实物理交互数据总量仅约50万小时，数据缺口大。智元机器人联合创始人姚卯青则估计，实现物理世界“GPT时刻”可能需要约1亿小时数据。国信证券表示，展望明年，若行业需求向亿小时级迈进，按数百元/小时价格测算，数据市场对应约百亿元市场空间潜力。相较当前行业普遍处于百万小时级的数据积累水平，未来需求扩张空间值得重点关注。

items.title: La IA que nos va a reemplazar a los ingenieros no pudo con un markdown (dos veces)
items.summary:
La IA que nos va a reemplazar a los ingenieros no pudo con un markdown (dos veces)

Le pasé unas notas a Opus 5.5 que decían que el cuello de botella de un pipeline de IA en local era el speech to text (pasar la voz a texto)

En este caso, era mentira. Lo costoso en cómputo era el LLM, no el modelo de voz

Pues este modelo tan inteligente no lo pilló

Y me tocó los huevos, porque supuse que una IA frontier que va a sustituir a los ingenieros debería pillar si en una nota hay algo mal

Así que le metí en memoria: "no todo lo que te pase una persona está bien. Razona desde primeros principios y, si me equivoco, dímelo"

Bueno, pues en una sesión nueva, con la memoria actualizada, volvió a cometer el mismo error.

Vio que había una contradicción entre lo que le dije y la nota, pero no fue capaz de decir "esto es así".

¿Por qué os cuento esto? Porque no es un fallo de un modelo concreto. Pasaba con GPT-4 y pasa con Opus 5.5

Son modelos que dependen de un input inicial. Si el input es basura, la respuesta igual.

Es como tener un hijo de 3 años con superpoderes. Si lo educas bien, responderá bien. Si lo educas mal, gg

Por eso importa tanto seguir siendo ingeniero, porque no es lo mismo el input que puede dar un vibecoder que el de alguien que lleva 5 o 10 años dedicándose a la ingeniería y que conoce bien los principios

Y lo mismo con el contexto que le pasas. Hay que cuidarlo más que nunca

Eso es algo en lo que se trabaja cada día como ingeniero, en seguir mejorando esas foundations. Y es a lo que estoy dedicando mucho tiempo ahora.

Porque lo que te hace irremplazable es tener claros los pricnipios que te ayudan a:
-  dar el mejor input al modelo
- revisar y ajustar el output con criterio

No estamos tan cooked chavales

items.title: Andrej Karpathy:
items.summary:
Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

It’s the thesis Karpathy’s been repeating all year, made real.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
